title: Witkoff and Kushner Meet Putin in Moscow as Ukraine Talks Restart
dek: US envoys met Putin in Moscow and Zelenskyy in Dublin. Witkoff says Europeans will join the next round, while Putin proposed a humanitarian evacuation from contested Kostiantynivka.
author: Meridian Newsroom

image.alt: The Senate Palace of the Kremlin in Moscow

keyPoints: Witkoff and Kushner met Zelenskyy in Dublin after the Kremlin meeting; Kyiv Independent reported the talks took place at Casement Aerodrome, a military base west of Dublin.
Witkoff told Russian state TV after meeting Putin that European negotiators would join the next round of talks, the BBC reported.
Putin proposed a temporary "humanitarian mission" in Kostiantynivka, which he said Russia controls, for the 400 to 500 people he said remain in the town, Kyiv Independent reported.
Ukraine rejects Moscow’s claim to control Kostiantynivka; presidential adviser Dmytro Lytvyn warned the proposal could be used to rotate troops.
Zelenskyy said Ukraine faced "systematic" Starshield restrictions, which the BBC reported hamper interception of Russian jet-powered drones.
body:
U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Russian President Vladimir Putin at the Kremlin on Thursday, going directly from the airport to a meeting that lasted just over two hours, the Washington Times reported. The Kremlin meeting followed two days of U.S.-mediated talks between Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi that ended Wednesday without a major breakthrough, the [Associated Press reported](https://www.npr.org/2026/11/12/nx-s1-6038809/us-envoys-meet-putin-russia-ukraine-war-talks).

The Abu Dhabi talks were the first direct discussions between Moscow and Kyiv in nine months, AP reported, held as U.S. diplomacy on the war had stalled.

## What came out of the meeting

Neither side has released a detailed readout. Before the meeting, Russian presidential aide Yuri Ushakov said it would address "various issues leading to a durable settlement of the crisis around Ukraine," [Meduza reported](https://meduza.io/en/feature/2026/11/12/kushner-and-witkoff-hold-talks-with-putin-before-heading-to-meet-zelensky-as-europe-seeks-a-seat-at-the-peace-talks).

After the meeting, Ushakov said Russia and the United States had agreed to continue trilateral negotiations, [CNN reported](https://us.cnn.com/2026/11/12/politics/ukraine-witkoff-kushner-putin-peace-talks-intl). He also said Putin would continue talks on Ukraine with President Donald Trump at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in China later this month, [TIME reported](https://time.com/article/2026/11/12/ukraine-russia-peace-deal-talks-putin-zelensky-witkoff-kushner/).

Witkoff told reporters, "I think progress was made," and said, "We've restarted it. We've set a new meeting." TIME quoted him saying this is "what President [Donald] Trump wants to see." There was no immediate comment from Kushner or Witkoff on the discussion, the Washington Times reported.

## Europe's seat at the table

Kushner said one goal of the Moscow meeting was to get Putin's blessing for European representatives to take part in the talks, AP reported. Witkoff said a European representative would be present for the next stage, which is expected to address the continent's wider security arrangements. "They're our partners, and it's important for them to be involved," he said, according to TIME.

Russian officials have rejected letting Europe into the talks. They argue that Europe has not presented a formal proposal to Moscow and that European financial support for Ukraine is slowing diplomacy, the Washington Times reported.

## Kostiantynivka proposal

Putin proposed a temporary "humanitarian mission" in Kostiantynivka, a Donetsk Oblast town that Russia claims to control, during Thursday’s meeting with the envoys. Putin said 400 to 500 people remained in the town and suggested a pause in fighting would let them leave, [Kyiv Independent reported](https://kyivindependent.com/witkoff-kushner-arrive-in-moscow-following-ukraine-peace-talks/). He also called for reciprocal steps, including demining, if Ukrainian forces still hold the town, and said Russia would need five days to clear access roads.

On Friday, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov said Russia is ready to carry out the operation if it receives appropriate security guarantees, following the model used in Oleshky last month. He urged the United States and Europe to press Ukraine to accept it, [the Moscow Times reported](https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2026/11/13/kremlin-says-ready-for-civilian-evacuation-from-ukraines-kostiantynivka-a94257/pdf). Ukraine’s human rights ombudsman, Dmytro Lubinets, said Kostiantynivka "was not even mentioned" among places where similar missions could be organized.

Ukraine has rejected Russia’s claim to control the town, and its General Staff said its forces continue operating against Russian infantry trying to infiltrate it. Lytvyn said the Oleshky operation had been used to rotate troops under cover of a ceasefire, and said the same was likely in Kostiantynivka.

## Witkoff’s account on Europe, and Dublin

Witkoff told Russian state television after meeting Putin that European negotiators would take part in the next round of trilateral talks, [the BBC reported](https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cwrkgmymk55zo). "They are our partners and it’s important to us that they take part," Witkoff said. The same report said a new round of trilateral talks had been agreed with Putin.

That account differs from the Nov. 12 reporting above, which said Moscow had resisted European participation. Meridian did not find a Kremlin confirmation of the European point in the sources reviewed, so both accounts are attributed to their sources.

On Thursday morning, Zelenskyy said Ukraine’s military was again facing "systematic" restrictions on Starshield, the military-grade satellite service developed by SpaceX, which made it harder to intercept Russian jet-powered drones, the BBC reported.

## The prisoner exchange

After Abu Dhabi, Russia and Ukraine agreed in principle to what Kushner called "the biggest humanitarian release of prisoners" of the war. Kushner said the numbers would be finalized Thursday, AP reported. NPR reported that the exact figure was still to be announced. Meridian has not seen a confirmed final number from either government and will update this story when one is published.

## Kyiv's concerns and next steps

Kyiv has complained, unofficially, that the focus of the talks has shifted from ending the war toward questions about the future architecture of European security. Meduza, citing RBC-Ukraine sources, reported that the Russian delegation refused to discuss a ceasefire, territory, energy or Black Sea security on the second day of the Abu Dhabi talks.

Witkoff and Kushner were scheduled to fly to Dublin to brief Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, AP reported. Zelenskyy said the day before that he was skeptical the envoys would return from Moscow with anything concrete, Meduza reported.

## Putin’s stated position

Putin told Witkoff and Kushner that any European troops sent to Ukraine after a ceasefire would be “absolutely unacceptable,” and that Russia would regard their deployment as a security threat and legitimate targets. “In other words, the war would resume immediately,” he said, according to the AP.

Putin also said Russia regards the border with Ukraine that a prospective peace deal would seal as extending to the four Ukrainian regions Moscow annexed in 2022 but never fully controlled, the AP reported.

Kushner said one goal of the meeting was to get Putin’s agreement that European representatives could join the talks on the continent’s broader security arrangements. Moscow has resisted that. Kushner said the Russian and Ukrainian delegations in Abu Dhabi “agreed on many of the principles, but are still apart on some of the way to accomplish” peace.

Meridian did not find a published Kremlin readout of Thursday’s meeting in the sources reviewed; the Kremlin account in this story comes from the AP and Russian aide Yuri Ushakov’s comments reported by CNN.

## Dublin talks

After the Kremlin meeting, Witkoff and Kushner traveled to Dublin to meet Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy, the BBC reported. Kyiv Independent reported that the meeting took place at Casement Aerodrome, a military base in Baldonnel, west of Dublin.

The BBC reported that Prime Minister Andy Burnham had said UK national security adviser Jonathan Powell would join the Dublin talks, but Downing Street later said his attendance had been delayed. Witkoff said a new round of trilateral talks had already been agreed with Putin.

The BBC also reported that Zelenskyy, speaking before the Dublin meeting, said the Starshield restrictions were ongoing and "helping the Russians kill more Ukrainians," and that Ukraine was trying to resolve the issue with the American side. The BBC noted that Russia’s position on territory has not shifted, based on Putin’s comments and Kremlin statements.
